literal: Even if it is cooked gruel made of clear water, than eating that which was yielded by one's own effort, a sweeter thing there is not.
translation: Even if it is mere gruel cooked with clear water, there is nothing sweeter than eating that which is earned by one's own effort.
modern: தெளிந்த நீரால் சமைக்கப்பட்ட கஞ்சி என்றாலும், தன் முயற்சியால் கிடைத்ததை உண்பதை விட இனிமையானது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the sweetness of self-reliance and honest labor. The poet compares a simple, watery gruel (தெண்ணீர் அடுபுற்கை) earned through one's own effort (தாள் தந்தது) to any other food. Eating what is obtained by one's own exertion is described as the sweetest experience, far superior to living on charity or begging. The key words 'தாள்' (effort) and 'உண்ணலின் ஊங்கினிய தில்' (nothing is sweeter than eating) emphasize that independence brings unmatched joy and dignity.
